summary: Dedicated pool throughput degradation caused by a single tenant's long-lived slow-consumption streams draining allocator credits
description:
Issue summary: Between 2026-03-01 09:00 and 11:30 PST LexiAI reported sustained p95/p99 throughput degradation on their dedicated pool. Impact: customer-visible throughput drop (20-50% lower completed tokens/sec for bursty batched routes) and increased 429s during peak window. Environment: dedicated reserved cluster in us-west-2.

Observed behavior: The degradation correlated with a small set (~3) of long-lived client connections from the LexiAI SDK that were consuming responses very slowly (client-side throttling) and repeatedly leaving in-flight microbatches open for 10-30s. This held allocator credits and effectively reduced the pool's available concurrency. Autoscaler responded by spinning up additional workers then later shrinking; result: oscillation and overall lower throughput.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Open 3 persistent streaming sessions to model redwood/open-llama-7b.
2) Send small batched prompts every 500ms but intentionally read responses slowly (10s drain).
3) Observe GPU slot counts drop and p95 token throughput fall after 10-15 minutes.

Attached/logs: kernel scheduler trace snippet, allocator credit timeline, per-tenant connection histogram (provided in attachments), and partial request traces showing long-lived KV cache pins. Key metrics: allocator_free_credits per-pool fell from 1200 -> 200 over 30 minutes; avg slot utilization stayed high but effective concurrency dropped; autoscaler add/remove events every ~8 minutes.

Initial customer impact: LexiAI production service experienced increased request queuing and some timed-out inference requests; they are on a dedicated contract and requested immediate mitigation.
comments: 2026-03-01 09:12 - Support (Priya): Triage started after customer alert. Gathering logs and asking for connection patterns and SDK version.

2026-03-01 09:28 - Customer (LexiAI - Aaron): Provided player logs and sample SDK trace showing long response-read delays and SDK v2.3.3. Noted behavior started after a change to their response buffer handling.
2026-03-01 10:05 - SRE (Ethan): Observed matching allocator credit drain. Opening investigation docket; temporarily bumped pool soft limits to free some capacity while we investigate.

2026-03-01 12:40 - Engineering (Maya): Noted autoscaler oscillation triggered by perceived sustained high active requests; hypothesizing slow consumer pattern keeps slots reserved and prefetch backlog grows.
2026-03-03 08:10 - Customer (Aaron): Applied SDK patch to drain responses faster; saw partial improvement but throughput not fully recovered.

2026-03-05 14:22 - SRE (Ethan): Implemented short-term tenant shaping policy (rate limit concurrent streaming sessions to 6) and scheduled allocator circuit-breaker PR for rollout. Monitoring for stabilization.
2026-03-05 16:01 - Support (Priya): Updated customer with mitigations and next steps.
investigation_notes: Checked allocator logs: observed steady decline in 'allocator_free_credits' corresponding to long-lived in-flight microbatches from lexiai-tenant-id. Credits not reclaimed until client connections closed or until scheduler eviction window (30s) fired.
Traceroutes and socket stats: 3 persistent streaming sockets showed average read latency >9s; connection keepalives present. No packet loss detected at the node level.

Autoscaler behavior: policy uses active_request_count and avg_slot_utilization; slow consumers keep active_request_count high while throughput low, causing autoscaler to add workers then later remove them (hysteresis mismatch).
Served model conditions: KV cache pins grew for the tenant; memory pressure forced downstream prefetch to queue leading to serialization of batch assignment.

Hypotheses: (A) slow client consumption pattern from LexiAI is holding allocator credits and prefetch windows open; (B) autoscaler hysteresis thresholds are too sensitive to active_request_count in presence of long-lived streams; (C) serving-runtime lacks an early reclaim for excessively slow stream reads.
resolution: Mitigations applied (short-term): 1) Tenant-shaping: limit concurrent persistent streaming sessions per-tenant to 6 and enforce a soft 8s streaming read threshold to allow early reclaim. 2) Temporarily increased pool soft limit to absorb backlog while shaping took effect. 3) Customer applied SDK fix to aggressively drain response buffer and lowered client read timeout. Result: throughput recovered ~85% of baseline within 90 minutes.

Permanent / planned fixes: 1) Allocator circuit-breaker PR (github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/4821) to detect and reclaim credits held by streams exceeding configurable read latency. 2) Autoscaler tuning: incorporate effective token-generation-rate metric (tokens/sec) in addition to active_request_count to avoid adding workers for slow-consumption patterns. 3) Add telemetry alert for 'long-lived-streams-per-tenant' to catch regression early. Target ETA: phased rollout starting 2026-03-18.

Follow-ups for customer: LexiAI to upgrade SDK to v2.3.4 which includes recommendations for streaming buffer drain patterns; Redwood to run a joint load test to confirm shaping parameters. Scheduled call 2026-03-06 11:00 PT.
Postmortem actions: Create runbook entry for 'slow-client-stream credit drain' with remediation steps and include sample SDK snippets for safe streaming consumption.
